summary.headline: FY26 total income rose to INR 1,279 crore with 12.3% revenue growth; net debt/EBITDA ~3x (3.07x) and FY27 revenue guided at 10-11%.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue growth was 12.3% against a 9-11% guidance band, with same-store RevPAR up 9.5%, despite several one-off disruptions that cut revenue by an estimated INR 45-52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA rose 8.8% to INR 463 crore at a 36.2% margin, and the GST slab change weighed on H2 margins. Q4 EBITDA fell 6% YoY to about INR 120 crore, which management attributes to GST, FF&E charges, pre-opening costs and the Middle East conflict hitting March revenue. Net debt fell to INR 1,450 crore after the GIC infusion, and a deferred tax credit of about INR 330 crore lifted reported PAT to about INR 567 crore. Management guided FY27 same-store revenue growth of 9-10% and total revenue growth of 10-11%, and a 38%-plus group margin.

financial_highlights.change: -6% YoY; ~INR 149 crore adjusted for one-offs (+16.8% YoY)
Includes ~INR 330 crore deferred tax income in Q4 and ~INR 83 crore impairment reversal; includes gain on Caspia Delhi sale

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow FY26 (after interest and lease MG)

segments.name: Core markets (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, Delhi NCR)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 76% of asset income in FY26. Delhi NCR same-store RevPAR declined about 9%; management expects mid-teens growth there in FY27 as Hyatt Place Gurgaon renovation completed by end-Q3 FY26.

segments.name: Upscale and upper-upscale portfolio
segments.commentary: Upscale hotels run at upwards of 42-43% margins; Holiday Inn Express margins at 41-42%. Incremental pipeline is weighted to upscale, limiting exposure to sub-INR 7,500 room rates.

segments.name: Asset recycling and non-core hotels
segments.commentary: Monetised 4 non-core hotels for INR 210 crore at about 20x EV/EBITDA over three years. Target now INR 200-250 crore over the next two years; Caspia Delhi was sold for INR 63 crore with EBITDA of about INR 1.5-2 crore.

segments.name: RARE India (experiential leisure)
segments.commentary: Acquired 70% stake in a curated platform of 73 hotels and about 1,000 rooms; under discussion for affiliation with Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 same-store revenue growth expected at 9-10%; total revenue growth underwritten at 10-11% with caution given the Middle East crisis, versus about 14% if no crisis.
Group EBITDA margin guided at about 38%, with 38%-plus maintained through the year; management says margins should reach 40%-plus on a normalised basis over time.
GST impact is permanent in absolute terms and has been about INR 7.5 crore YoY in Q3 and about INR 10 crore in Q4; normalises from Q3 FY27 on a YoY basis.
FY27 interest expense about INR 127 crore on existing debt; guided at INR 135-140 crore including a 15-20 bps rate-hardening assumption.
Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise at about 2.5x in 12-18 months; currently 3.07x.
FY27 capex INR 250-270 crore (about INR 150 crore for W Hyderabad, opening at end-FY27); FY28 similar run-rate, mainly Westin Bangalore. Total pipeline capex about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
capex_capacity: W Hyderabad (HITEC City) to open at end-FY27; expected to add about 6-7% revenue growth on a run-rate basis from FY28.
Pipeline openings: Tribute Bangalore Whitefield at end-FY28; Westin Bangalore Whitefield, Ingka Noida (162 rooms, variable lease) and Marriott Stiperumbudur (135 rooms, Chennai) in FY29-FY30.
Navi Mumbai 700-room Westin and Fairfield project announced; One Financial District Hyderabad (260 rooms) under development. Management excluded both from revenue and EBITDA forecasts.
GIC platform: INR 750 crore for a 35% stake in a 1,000-room upscale platform; INR 600 crore received, INR 150 crore balance over about two years linked to Westin Tribute Bangalore capex.
Over five years FY27-FY31, free cash of about INR 1,550 crore (flat base) plus about INR 1,000 crore from same-store growth; more than INR 3,000 crore cumulative after new openings, per management.
demand_pricing: QTD revenue growth (April-May 2026) is double-digit; April was flattish and May strong, against a weak May 2025 base affected by Operation Sindoor.

Q4 revenue growth ran about 12% through February before the Middle East conflict pulled March to below -1%; interrupted by the India-Pakistan conflict (May), August floods, December airline disruption and March Middle East conflict.
One-off disruptions cut FY26 revenue by INR 45-52 crore; management says underlying growth would have been 16-17%.
Management says inbound and long-haul travel is recovering (including US); repricing expected to restart as business rebalances. Occupancy described as strong.
Bangalore: about 17,000-18,000 rooms; supply growth about 5-5.5% CAGR, with more than half of future supply concentrated on the airport-Hebbal corridor where SAMHI has no presence.

Median flow-through about 55%, with 55%-plus expected; a Q4 margin drag came from a low-margin outdoor and corporate catering contract at Hyatt Regency Pune (about INR 13-14 crore), which management says ends from May 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How are April and May trending, and what is FY27 like-for-like growth after a favourable FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: QTD growth is double-digit: April flattish, May strong against a weak May 2025 base. Management expects YoY growth to stay in double digits through Q1 FY27 despite the Gulf crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST be a permanent margin reduction, and what margins are expected in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: GST impact is permanent in absolute terms, but management expects about 38% group margin, 38%-plus through the year, as pipeline is upscale with few rooms below INR 7,500.

qa_highlights.question: Is there construction delay risk, and will the focus shift to acquisitions or asset recycling?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating and growth teams are separate. Acquisitions stay opportunistic, guided by discount-to-replacement-cost, mid-teens ROCE and no long-lead greenfield. Asset recycling will continue with a few more candidates identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook including new openings, and the interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Same-store growth of 9-10% plus about 3-4% incremental from renovated assets; total about 14% if no crisis. Guided at 10-11% for caution. Interest guided at INR 135-140 crore including rate hardening.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not improve in Q4 and what is the GST drag and lease accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a low-margin catering contract (INR 13-14 crore revenue) that ends from May. GST drag is about INR 3 crore on a YoY basis per management's arithmetic. Variable lease payments (1.5-2% of revenue) go through P&L; lease-treatment impact on EBITDA margins is about 150-170 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE target, net debt/EBITDA path and capex funding for FY31?
qa_highlights.answer: Current asset pool can deliver 14-15% ROCE. Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise around 2.5x in 12-18 months. Free cash base of about INR 310 crore assumed flat; management assumes no operating leverage and no EBITDA from Navi Mumbai or One Financial District; W Hyderabad and Ingka expected to add INR 400-500 crore EBITDA by FY31.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: March revenue fell below -1% YoY and the effect is still continuing into April; management says it may keep affecting Q1 FY27 absolute numbers.
GST slab change (12% with input credit to 5% without) is permanent; margin dilution persists and sub-INR 7,500 room sales could rise in crisis periods.
Interest-rate hardening: management has assumed 15-20 bps rise; currency weakness is cited as a risk.
Bangalore supply: heavy Outer Ring Road and airport-Hebbal supply could pressure occupancy, which management says has already taken a hit over recent quarters.
Execution risk on pipeline (W Hyderabad end-FY27, Tribute and Westin Bangalore, Navi Mumbai greenfield) and capex of about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
Capital allocation: a Board-level discussion on buybacks or shareholder returns is ongoing with no commitment; asset recycling could extend to minority dilution at asset level (not committed).
Deferred tax income of about INR 330 crore is non-cash; reported PAT is inflated by one-offs and is not a run-rate measure.
key_quotes: So we do expect a 55%-plus flow-through. 50% is underwhelming, 60% is where we arc happy.
We're running really strong capacity utilization across the group.
Notwithstanding the share price or the discount Viraj, we are under a fiduciary obligation to create sharcholder value and allocate capital
But I think the discipline will decide what we do in future.
So I think structurally, the company will secure its place at 40%-plus reported margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term plan: management repeatedly underwrites 9-11% same-store revenue growth, 2.5x leverage and the INR 2,200 crore capex, and says upside exists. Cautious on the near term, citing the Middle East conflict, GST permanence and rate hardening, and it deflects on acquisitions, buybacks and asset-level minority dilution, which it treats as uncommitted.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 total revenue growth of 10-11% (same-store 9-11%), backed by QTD double-digit growth, repricing expected as travel recovers and the W Hyderabad hotel opening at end-FY27 (INR 150 crore capex), though the largest pipeline openings fall in FY28-FY30 and the guidance is caveated by the Middle East crisis.
